brand_kit_extractions.src/lib/visual/queries.ts: The only store for a brand-extraction run.

brand_visual_identity.src/lib/visual/queries.ts: The only store for a client's visual identity — a whole-row upsert at extraction and a blob patch for edits.

client_ideas.src/features/ideas/lib/ideas.ts: The whole client-ideas lifecycle (submit, status, link to post, mark read) in one file.

client_sources.src/features/sources/actions/source-acti: The source manager's CRUD. createSource and updateSource both resolve the URL through resolveSourceUrl — they did not, and updateSource was a live SSRF hole until 2026-08-31.
reportStatus stamps last_fetched_at / last_fetch_status / last_fetch_error after a fetch. Fetch health, written by the fetcher; it never touches a source's configuration.
client_sources.src/lib/clients/sync-source-pillars.ts: removeDeletedPillarIds writes ONE column, pillar_ids, as a cascade of a pillar deletion — reachable only through updateBrandProfile, never from the sources screen. updateSource writes the same column when the user scopes a source, which is a different operation. (An earlier note here said 'config' and called this open audit business; both were wrong.)

client_style_memos.src/ai/learning/distill-style-memo.ts: The memo's only writer, next to the distiller that produces it.

clients.src/features/clients/actions/client-acti: create, update and delete from the clients screen.
clients.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. Its only caller is createClient, the onboarding flow in both modes.

discarded_drafts.src/lib/queries/discarded-drafts.ts: One insert for both discard sources (wizard, review). reason stays optional — distill-style-memo filters on it being non-null.

generation_runs.src/lib/generation/runs.ts: start and finish, paired in one file so a run cannot be opened without a way to close it.

generation_themes.src/lib/generation/runs.ts: Themes belong to a run and are tracked beside it.

idea_form_tokens.src/features/ideas/lib/ideas.ts: getOrCreateToken — the idea form's link, minted beside the ideas it collects.

ig_account_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/instagram/acc: upsertAccountMetricDays — the only writer. There were six inline upserts across sync-metrics, refresh-window and online-followers, each restating the onConflict target. Callers write PARTIAL rows on purpose (reach in one pass, day totals in another, online-follower hours in a third) so no pass nulls a column another owns; that is why this is a thin shared upsert and not a whole-row writer.
ig_account_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/purge-: purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table for Meta's data-deletion callback and an account switch; deleteClient deliberately leans on the `clients` cascade instead. This was hand-listed until the delete went through a `scoped(table)` helper that hid `.from(table)` from the scan; the deletes are written out now, so the scan finds them and this entry is checked like any other.

ig_audience_snapshots.src/features/analytics/lib/instagram/syn: syncDemographicsWeekly, beside the sync that fetches it.

intelligence_briefings.src/features/dashboard/lib/write-briefin: writeWeeklyBriefing — the one writer: the global weekly brief, one row per week_start, upserted with ignoreDuplicates as the claim against a racing cron tick.

notifications.src/components/layout/shell-context.tsx: The browser toggling is_read for the signed-in user, optimistically. Read state only — it can never create a notification, and it is RLS-scoped rather than admin.
notifications.src/lib/notifications/notify.ts: notify() — the only insert. There were five, four bypassing the dedup. Cooldown is a per-caller decision (NOTIFY_EVERY_TIME), not blanket: two approval emails in a week are two events.

post_approval_tokens.src/features/approval-portal/lib/approva: createApprovalBatch mints the week's tokens, clearing any superseded batch first.
post_approval_tokens.src/features/approval-portal/actions/app: submitApproval records the client's decision on the token they arrived with.
post_approval_tokens.src/lib/actions/post-actions.ts: resolveChangeRequest closes a change request from the agency side.

post_canvas_docs.src/lib/canvas/doc-store.ts: upsertCanvasDoc for an edit, insertCanvasDocs when a post is created with docs already made.

post_history.src/lib/queries/post-history.ts: recordPostTopics — the cron batch and the approve route both record topics, and were writing the identical row from two files until 2026-08-31.

post_images.src/features/assets/lib/storage.ts: putPostImage / putPostImages — the only way an image lands at a position. There were four, three of which deleted the row and its file before inserting, so a failed insert lost the picture.
post_images.src/app/api/posts/[id]/images/route.ts: DELETE removes a slide the user deleted. A removal, not a write of an image — it has no row to put.

posting_schedules.src/features/clients/actions/client-acti: createClient seeds it; updateSchedule is the schedule editor.
posting_schedules.src/features/clients/lib/provision-clien: provisionClient — the ONE way a client and its mandatory children are created. Its only caller is createClient, the onboarding flow in both modes.

post_publications.src/features/publishing/lib/publication-: The ONE writer, with seven operations: createPublications records where a post is going, withdrawPendingPublications drops the destinations of a post pulled off the calendar (only ones that have not gone out, so unscheduling cannot erase that it published), claimPublication takes a destination for an attempt, setPublishRef persists the reference a network handed back, markPublicationPublished and markPublicationFailed record the outcome, and rearmPublication is the only place attempts are reset. They are in one file BY DESIGN — they are the states of one lifecycle.

posts.src/lib/actions/post-actions.ts: The agency's edits: updatePost (nine validated columns), savePostCopy (caption and slides, partial — the calendar saves a caption with no slides), persistRewrite, schedulePosts, deletePost, duplicatePostAsDraft (a published post reused as a fresh draft, through draftColumns — never a mutation of the published row, whose publications carry the ids the network knows it by).
posts.src/app/api/posts/route.ts: POST creates a post from an approved wizard draft, through draftColumns.
posts.src/app/api/cron/generate/route.ts: The nightly batch inserts generated drafts, through the same draftColumns.
posts.src/app/api/posts/[id]/publish/route.ts: Publish-now stamps the slot on a post published straight from the unscheduled tray — scheduled_at plus the status statusForSlot pairs with it — because the cron's backstop window only selects rows that have one. It writes nothing else: the claim, the attempt counter and the outcome are the publication's, in publication-store.ts.
posts.src/features/calendar/actions/post-recov: rearmFailedPublication — the user putting a failed destination back in the queue. It writes the post's SLOT (scheduled_at with the status statusForSlot pairs with it) and nothing else; the attempt counter it used to reset belongs to the publication now, in rearmPublication.
posts.src/app/api/cron/visuals/route.ts: The visuals lane's own attempt counter and status, which is separate from the publish counter on purpose.
posts.src/lib/visual/post-color.ts: claimScheme — a compare-and-swap on visual_ground/visual_accent so two lanes generating one carousel cannot split its colours.

social_connections.src/features/publishing/lib/refresh-toke: Rotates an expiring Instagram token without the user (update by id, never touching account identity). Retiring a dead one is retireConnection in lib/meta/connection-store.ts — this file only calls it.
social_connections.src/app/api/meta/data-deletion/route.ts: Meta's data-deletion callback erases the connection. Required by the platform and deliberately unconditional.
social_connections.src/app/api/canva/callback/route.ts: Stores the Canva connection from its OAuth flow.
social_connections.src/app/api/canva/canva-auth.ts: Refreshes the Canva token. Separate provider, separate lifetime, separate refresh endpoint.
social_connections.src/features/settings/actions/canva-acti: The user disconnecting Canva. Uses the service-role client BY NECESSITY: the only policy on this table is keyed on client_id, and a Canva row is owned by a user so its client_id is NULL — a user-scoped delete would match nothing and report success. Ownership is proven in TypeScript instead; see the comment at the call site.
social_connections.src/features/settings/actions/team-actio: removeTeamMember takes the departing member's personal integrations with them. Distinct from disconnectCanvaConnection (that is the owner choosing to unlink); this is the workspace removing someone. Added 2026-08-31 because social_connections.user_id is NO ACTION, so removing a member who held a Canva connection raised 23503 and surfaced as a message the admin could not act on.
social_connections.src/lib/meta/connection-store.ts: storeConnection — the ONE writer of "store the connection an OAuth flow just produced". Three flows produce one: Instagram Business Login, the Facebook user token that lists a person's Pages, and the Page they then pick. They differ in what they connect, not in how it is recorded, so they share the write rather than carrying three upserts with three conflict targets. Client-scoped rows conflict on (client_id, platform); user-scoped ones on (user_id, platform), with a NULL client_id that also puts them outside RLS — so every read of those keeps its platform filter. A successful connect also clears retired_at / retired_reason (migration 20260850) and last_sync_error — it is the operation that ends a retirement. retireConnection is the ONE writer of the opposite operation, "retire a token Meta has declared dead": access_token = null plus retired_at / retired_reason, by (client_id, platform).
social_connections.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/sync-s: recordSyncHealth stamps last_sync_at / last_sync_error — the only writer of a sync VERDICT (storeConnection clears last_sync_error on a fresh connect, which is the other operation on that column; see OPERATIONS.md). It never touches a token. It updates by (client_id, platform), which is exactly one row: social_connections_client_id_platform_key makes that pair UNIQUE — the same index the meta callback's onConflict relies on.

users.src/lib/auth/create-user-record.ts: The user row is created with the account, with the email guard — that column is a lookup key and a blank one is an account nobody can recover.

syncClientComments — the half-hourly capture, and the only writer that brings comments IN. Upserts on Instagram's own comment id and deletes rows the API stopped returning for a post it just refetched, which is how an upstream delete reaches us.
platform_comments.src/features/comments/actions/comment-ac: The three moderation actions, each recording the change it just made on Instagram: a reply inserts its own row so the comment reads as answered now rather than after the next cron, hide flips the flag, delete removes the comment and its replies. Not a second sync — the same fact the cron would have brought back, written early by the party that caused it.
platform_comments.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/purge-: purgeAccountAnalytics erases the audience's comments alongside the ig_* metrics — the part of Meta's data-deletion callback that actually erases third parties.

platform_post_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/post-m: upsertPostMetricRows — the only writer, for the same reason account-metrics-store is: two jobs now write this table and nothing else would keep their conflict target in step. Callers write PARTIAL rows on purpose — the nightly sync writes identity AND measurements, the half-hourly comments sync writes identity only (caption, permalink, thumbnail, post_id) because the queue renders the post a comment sits under and cannot wait until 03:30 for it. The comments sync must never write the measurement columns: a zero there is indistinguishable from a measured zero on the analytics page.
platform_post_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/purge-: purgeAccountAnalytics deletes this table for Meta's data-deletion callback and an account switch; deleteClient deliberately leans on the `clients` cascade instead. This was hand-listed until the delete went through a `scoped(table)` helper that hid `.from(table)` from the scan; the deletes are written out now, so the scan finds them and this entry is checked like any other.

fb_page_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/facebook/fb-p: upsertFbPageMetricDays is the one writer of a Page's daily metrics — a separate table from ig_account_metrics by decision (20260846): five shared columns did not justify squeezing Facebook concepts into Instagram-named ones.
fb_page_metrics.src/features/analytics/lib/shared/purge-: Deletes a Page's day rows as part of the Meta data-deletion cascade and the reconnect purge, beside the other analytics tables.
